history.note: Structural changes needed for the split (render unchanged): hero root id 'top' -> 'hero' (header wordmark href updated to #hero; footer anchors #educatie/#kanalen still on the .grp elements, #trackrecord moved from the .grp to the section root, same scroll position because the margin collapses through the section); '.grp:first-child{margin-top:0}' became '.roll > :first-child > .grp:first-child{margin-top:0}' since every .grp is now first child of its own <section>; the lightbox <dialog>+script moved inside #trackrecord (top layer, so .page{overflow:hidden} is irrelevant).

history.gap: The identity is a genre template, not a design: black ground, gradient-gold badge logo, gold-foil CTA repeated twice in the same viewport (header and hero), tracked mono labels, Playfair-italic tagline — every trading-Discord landing page looks exactly like this. At the bar the gold would be one hairline and one accent, the logo would sit as a mark not a poster, and the "De leerstof" grid would be cut for one consistent chart crop and scale instead of five mismatched TradingView screenshots (watermarks, wildly different candle zooms, right-hand chart running off its frame) with a centre spine that slices straight through the middle image of the 3-up row and through the CTA button, while caption "02 Fibonacci, equal highs en sellside liquidity" wraps to three lines of tracked caps.
history.motion: Six identical frames — no reveal, no parallax, no scroll response; the only change is a header re-render glitch in frame 2. Absence, not restraint.
history.verdict: B has a distinctive editorial voice — photographic atmosphere, dual clocks, quiet serif micro-type, a vertical mark, real scroll choreography — and even with its visible bugs it reads as a designed world; A is cleanly aligned but is a stock dark-and-gold trading template with a duplicated CTA, mismatched screenshot charts and a spine that cuts through its own content. Neither is shortlist-ready as-is, but B is a craft pass away from it while A needs a new idea.
